commercial_incentive: none evident; internal university training session (CSUSB Graduate Studies)
key_insights: CSUSB's graduate GPA cutoff was lowered from 3.0 to 2.5 (with appeals possible down to 2.0) after reviewing ~600 appeals/year and finding admitted 2.5-3.0 students performed similarly to those above 3.0
Presenter argues standardized test scores (GRE/GMAT) have only weak correlation with long-term graduate outcomes and recommends against using cutoff scores
Recommends reviewing non-cognitive variables (resilience, motivation, personal context via essays/interviews) before looking at GPA or test scores, reversing the typical review order
Discussion flags that these 'holistic' practices themselves can disadvantage first-generation students who don't know how to request strong letters or navigate the process
Recommends formal rubrics reviewed periodically against actual student outcomes data to confirm criteria still predict program success
specific_numbers_or_facts: CSU-wide minimum graduate GPA cutoff is 2.5, with appeals allowed down to 2.0 (presenter)
CSUSB's own graduate GPA cutoff was 3.0 until a few years before this recording, and was lowered after data review (presenter)
